result:
Changed files: `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh`, `tests/run_tests.sh`, and the new `lib/common.sh`.

Details:

- **rotate.sh** — the surplus list was `tail -n +"$keep"` on a chronologically ascending list, which deleted `total-keep+1` archives and, at exactly N, the newest. Now the oldest `total-keep` are deleted (`head -n`, guarded so `head -n 0` — not supported by BSD head — is never called), and the early exit uses `-le` so exactly-N prints "nothing to rotate".
- **verify.sh** — the sidecar file name was extracted with `awk '{print $2}'`, which truncated `my backup-…tar.gz` to `my`, so the archive looked missing → BAD. It now takes the digest as the first word and the whole remainder of the line as the name (`read -r expected file`); the digest comparison is also quoted `[[ ]]`.
- **lib/common.sh** — new file holding the shared option-parsing block (incl. `is_uint`, `need_value`, the `--keep` validation) and `resolve_dir`; `rotate.sh` and `verify.sh` source it with `"$@"` and keep all flags (`--dest/--dest=`, `--name`, `--keep`, `-q/--quiet`, `-n/--dry-run`, `-h/--help`, `--`, unknown-option handling — smoke-tested). `backup.sh`, `restore.sh`, `report.sh` are untouched.
- **tests/run_tests.sh** — added 3 checks: rotate with exactly N archives deletes nothing (the reported bug), rotate with N+1 deletes the oldest and keeps the newest N (catches the opposite-direction fix), and verify passes for `my backup-20260101-000000.tar.gz` (the space bug). One pre-existing expectation had a typo (it expected `demo-20260101-000000…` while the fixture stamps `120000`, so it failed even at the base commit); I corrected it to `120000`.

`bash tests/run_tests.sh` passes: 9/9, "all tests passed".
